core_obligations: Prepare the excellency input (proof lines 4057-4070): a complete Noetherian local ring is J-2, Nagata, excellent and has a dualizing complex, and the same holds for rings essentially of finite type over it; since completions of excellent local normal domains are normal, all the local rings met below have the required properties.

Set up the induction (proof lines 4072-4082): choose a regular complete local subring over which A is finite and argue by induction on the degree of the induced fraction field extension; the base case of degree one is the case of a regular ring.

Induction step through an intermediate field (proof lines 4084-4108): for an intermediate field take the integral closure B of the subring in it, choose a resolution of its spectrum by induction, and let X be the normalization of the base change to A; since A is J-2 the regular locus of X is open, so X is a normal surface with finitely many singular closed points, and at each of them the completed local ring is finite of smaller degree over the corresponding completion of Y, so has a resolution by induction.

Replace completions by blowups and finish (proof lines 4110-4152): the resolutions of the completed local rings of X correspond to a sequence of normalized blowups ending regular, and by the equivalence of sequences these combine into blowups making the surface normal with Gorenstein local rings; the remaining singularities are rational double points, whose resolution then completes the induction and the proof.
proof_roadmap: Record the excellency, Nagata and dualizing properties ensuring that all rings encountered behave well, including under completion.
Run an induction on the degree of the fraction field extension over a finite regular complete local subring.
In the induction step pass to an intermediate field, normalize the base change, and resolve the finitely many singularities of the completion by induction.
Convert resolutions of completions into normalized blowups and finish by resolving the resulting rational double points.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a normal two dimensional complete Noetherian local ring has a resolution of singularities (statement lines 4050-4055). The proof (proof lines 4057-4156) records the excellency properties of complete local rings, runs an induction on the degree of the fraction field extension over a finite regular complete local subring, and in the induction step uses an intermediate field, normalization of a base change, resolutions of the completions of the finitely many singular points, normalized blowups and the resolution of rational double points. H3: a long induction combining several chapter results with genuine reductions, written out in full.
